newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bloodshed returns to Algerian capital.
newsitem.headline: Bloodshed returns to Algerian capital.

text.p: A car bomb killed eight people and wounded 25 in Algiers, ripping through a crowded street outside a restaurant in El Biar on the heights of the Mediterranean city, Algerian newspapers said on Thursday.
The blast ended a two-week lull in reported serious attacks and bloodshed in the capital with an official population put at 2.6 million but which unofficially is estimated at four million.

Boys selling cigarettes, women heading home, customers in the restaurant and occupants of passing cars were hit by the explosion which Le Matin newspaper said coincided with an attack on a police patrol in another area.
The last big bomb in Algiers hit a market on July 14, killing at least 21 people and wounding about 40. Since then the violence has focused outside the capital.

In the past week, 170 people have been slaughtered in villages and isolated communities in rebel attacks that Algerian papers said were revenge for 300 rebel deaths in a military offensive against a mountain hideout earlier in July.
Algerian security forces, who blamed Moslem fundamentalists, gave an initial toll of three dead and 25 wounded after the bomb exploded at 7.40 p.m.(1840 GMT) on Wednesday.
Many of the wounded were in a serious condition.

"At the (hospital) emergency department were a dozen wounded who miraculously escaped death. Some were in a serious state and going to have surgery, including amputation of arms and/or legs," said Liberte newspaper.

From l'Universal restaurant on Boulevard Bougara, windows were shattered for some 400 yards (metres). The carcases of three burnt-out cars lay nearby. The occupants of a passing Renault were caught with its full force, said El Watan newspaper.

One woman, whose balcony overlooked the scene, was crying out for her mother who had vanished. A youth demanded of people on the spot: "Have you seen Moh (Mohamed), the redhead. I saw him a minute ago standing by the door to the bar."
The bomb exploded just hours after a policeman and a civilian were killed and two police wounded, in an attack in La Glaciere area against a mobile patrol, Le Matin newspaper said.
It said two "terrorists" armed with Kalashnikovs had been seen in the same district three days earlier.
The return of violence came just ahead of a new statute coming into force for the decaying, overcrowded city which now has its own ministerial-governor, Cherif Rahmani.
At a ceremony on Thursday, Rahmani said the new governorate of Great Algiers had been set up to "put a brake on the loss of authority by public bodies and re-gild the image of Algiers".

In his comments reported by the official Algerian news agency APS he made no mention of the killings which had forced Algiers to impose tough measures to try to thwart car bombs, such as no parking on busy roads, including Boulevard Bougara before 7 p.m.

In a reminder of the years in which violence has racked the country, a court just hours before Wednesday's bomb sentenced six journalists to suspended prison terms for a report carried in El Watan newspaper in January 1993.
Omar Belhouchet, director of El Watan, and Nacera Benali who wrote the report, were each sentenced to six months and four other journalists each to four months --all suspended.

Belhouchet's French-language newspaper, viewed as the best informed on security issues, had reported that an armed group had cut the throats of five gendarmes in Ksar El Hirane, in Laghouat province some 350 km (220 miles) south of Algiers.
He and the others were charged with "premature publication" and other offences, including threatening state security.
The violence had erupted the previous year, shortly after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
About 60,000 people have been killed since then. A fresh general election was held last June 5 but brought no letup.
Le Matin on Thursday said the latest bloodshed showed one thing: "The beast is wounded. And it can go still further in its murderous folly."
